text: Clara came home after a night shift at the hospital. The flat was cold, and she was afraid the pipes would freeze. A bucket stood under the window to catch a drip. "Please set the heating to nineteen degrees," she said to the thermostat. "And warm the bedroom first, I'm so tired." The assistant answered, "Heating is set to nineteen. The bedroom radiator is on now." Clara sat on the bed near the radiator and listened to it click. Then she said, "Turn it down to eighteen when I fall asleep." The assistant said it would lower the heat at ten o'clock. Clara was asleep before it did.

name: restart_printer
does: Restarts a stuck printer and checks that it has the minimum paper and ink to print, so nobody has to reach inside with a glove to fix it.
inputs: which printer to restart
people say:
- The printer is stuck again
- Nothing comes out when I press print
- Can you turn the printer off and on for me?
- My printer isn't answering
- It just blinks at me, please fix it

Someone packing upstairs, with a stream of music playing, wants to know when their flight to an island in the sea leaves on Friday morning.
when does my flight leave
flight time?
What time do I take off on Friday morning?
Tell me the departure time for my flight on Friday morning
Is my plane still going at the same time?
When should I be at the gate?
Could you please check what time my flight goes on Friday morning, so I can book a taxi?
I need to know what time I'm leaving

Person: I'm in a hurry. Move fifty euros please.
Assistant: Which account should I take it from, and where should it go?
Person: From savings to checking. I need to buy tea and medicine for my sick brother.
Assistant: Moving fifty euros from savings to checking. Is that right?
Person: Sorry, make it sixty.
Assistant: Done. Sixty euros moved from savings to checking.
Person: Thanks, bye.
Assistant: I hope your brother feels better soon.

Dana was nine years old, and the family speaker in the kitchen was her favourite thing. After school she pulled a chair up to the counter. "Make the volume lower and play this song in the living room too," she said. The speaker answered, "Okay, I made it quieter and now it is playing in the living room as well." Soon both speakers played the same song. Her big brother shouted something rude from the stairs about the noise, and Dana laughed. "Make the hall speaker quiet," she said. The speaker set the hall to zero, and Dana danced on her chair.

Someone slipped in the snow outside a cafe and now has an ugly cut on their hand and wants to know how to treat it.
cut help
My hand is bleeding, what do I do?
how to stop bleeding
What should I do about a cut that won't stop bleeding?
I got a nasty cut, how do I clean it?
Tell me what to do for a deep cut
Could you walk me through looking after a bad cut, please?
bleeding finger, help

When a family moves house, the post office needs to know the new address. This is called a change of address, and it makes sure letters find you in your new home. My grandfather forgot to do it, so his letters went to strangers for a month. People say things like "I've moved, send my mail to 4 Pine Road" or "Change where my bills go." They may also say, "Switch my electricity to the new house from Monday." The movers pack the boxes, but a dangerous thing like a can of gas must stay behind. On the first day, neighbours often welcome the new family with a cake.

Someone stirring rice in the kitchen, with a sore head and a tap that drips, wants quiet music playing.
play something calm
Put on soft music, nothing loud
music please, not rock
My head is sore, so no drums or shouting, just something gentle
Can you play some quiet songs? I don't want anything fast
Something slow, no singing
Play relaxing tunes but don't make them loud
I'd like background music that isn't too busy

Rosa had just moved to the city, and the air in her small flat felt heavy. A yellow haze hung over the street. She stretched her arms and asked her phone, "Is the air outside bad today?" The assistant said the air quality number was one hundred and fifty, which was unhealthy for people with weak lungs. Rosa nodded. "Then please turn on the air purifier and tell me when I should change the filter," she said. The assistant switched on the purifier in the bedroom and said the filter had about twenty days left. Rosa kept the windows shut, and by evening the air smelled cleaner.

Smart bulbs let you change a lamp without touching it. A light is for seeing, but also for mood. If you are sick in bed, a bright ceiling light hurts, so you want it low and warm. People say "Make it dimmer," "Turn the lamp to yellow," or "Switch off the bedroom light in five minutes." The bulb counts the minutes and then turns itself off, so you do not have to get up. Some people ask for a different colour for reading and another for the evening. Short words work well too: "brighter," "softer," "off."

Person: News.
Assistant: Which station would you like for the news?
Person: The local one. I just finished a night shift and my tablet is too difficult to use when I'm this tired. I keep trying to swipe to the radio app.
Assistant: No problem, I can do it. Do you want the city station or the regional one?
Person: City.
Assistant: Playing the city news station now.
Person: Louder.
Assistant: Okay, I turned the volume up. Is that good?
Person: Perfect, thank you.

Valentina was planning the big family dinner for the holidays. She sat in her armchair with an empty cup of tea and spoke to her tablet. "Remind me on Saturday to buy decorations," she said. Then she shook her head. "No, wait, Sunday. The shops close early on Saturday." The assistant said, "Okay, I changed the reminder to Sunday morning." Valentina smiled. Next she asked it to disconnect from the old speaker in the hall, because it was too loud, and to read a chapter of the story book to her grandchildren. The assistant did both, and the house became quiet and warm.

A voice note is a note you say out loud instead of typing. It is useful when your hands are busy or sore. I like to talk into my phone while I walk a mile to work, and the idea is saved for later. People say "Make a note: buy stamps," "Add milk to my shopping note," or "Find my note about the dentist." When a note is wrong, they say "Change the date in my last note to Friday" or "Delete that note." Old notes can be found by a word you remember, like "find the note with the word garden."

name: set_blinds
does: Opens or closes blinds and curtains in a room, even at a regular time, so the morning light comes in before the kettle boils.
inputs: which room, open or closed, how far, and the time if there is one
people say:
- Let the sun in the kitchen
- Close the curtains, it's too bright
- Open the bedroom blinds halfway
- Shut the blinds at seven tonight
- I can't see the TV, the glare is awful

A to-do list is a short list of things you need to do. Tom keeps his on his phone: buy one kilogram of apples, fix the dripping tap, and draw a square on the calendar for Saturday's party. When a task is done, he checks it off and it goes away. People change their lists all day. They say "Add call the bank to my list," "Move laundry to tomorrow," or "Put the dentist at the top." They also say "Tick off the tap," "What's still left today?" and "Remove the apples." A list helps you not to forget.

name: homework_tracker
does: Saves homework with due dates and tells you what is due next, so you can finish the ugly ones before the sunshine pulls you outside.
inputs: the subject, the task, and the due date
people say:
- What homework do I have this week?
- Write down that the history essay is due Friday
- Lock in an hour for maths tomorrow after school
- Which assignment is due first?
- I handed in the science project, take it off

Bo worked in a cold office, and the only warm thing was the cap on his head. At nine o'clock he spoke to the smart thermostat on the wall. "Set the office to twenty-two degrees," he said. The assistant answered that the building was divided into zones and that his zone was now heating up. Bo asked, "Keep it on for sixty minutes, then lower it a little." The assistant said, "Okay, twenty-two for the next hour, and then twenty." Soon his fingers felt better. Bo took off the cap and went back to his email.

Alessandro ran a small bookshop, and every winter the front room got cold. One Monday morning a student came in shivering. "Turn the heating up to twenty and switch off the heater in the back room," Alessandro said to the shop assistant app on his phone. "Okay, the front is now set to twenty, and the back heater is off," it answered. Then he added, "Label the new thermostat Front Shop." "Done," said the assistant. "The name is saved. Is that correct?" Alessandro checked the screen and nodded. The student sat down with a book, warm at last.

Person: I want to go swimming at the beach after my shift tomorrow. Is it safe?
Assistant: Which beach do you mean?
Person: Shell Bay. I'm going with my husband.
Assistant: Shell Bay has calm water tomorrow, and the tide is going out at five. The water is about eighteen degrees.
Person: Good. Last time I got crispy in the sun. How much more sun cream should I use?
Assistant: I can't give medical advice, sorry. The label on the bottle says to put it on again every two hours and after swimming.
Person: Okay, I'll do double the usual and bring a hat.

Colin had ten quick minutes before the school run. His daughter Ivy had to practice her violin, and the kitchen was a mess. "Play Ivy's practice playlist and turn the volume down a little," he said to the speaker. The assistant answered right away, "Playing Ivy's practice playlist at a lower volume." Soft violin music filled the room. Ivy tapped her foot and played along with the second song. Colin found her shoes under the table and her bag by the door. When the song ended, he asked the speaker to stop the music, and they walked to school together.

A work meeting is a call where people meet on a screen. Before it starts, someone posts the agenda in the chat, so everyone knows what will be talked about. To join, you open the link in your email and press the join button. People change small things all the time. They say "Mute my microphone," "Share my screen," or "Turn my camera off." Some like a picture behind them, like a butterfly or a blue sky. At the end, people say "Leave the meeting" or "Send me the notes." A good meeting is short and clear.

Dragan was a retired teacher, and on Thursdays he looked after his grandson Luka. The boy dropped his boots by the door, a pair of muddy green ones, and ran to the table. "Excuse me," Dragan said to the assistant on his phone, "could you please set a reminder for four o'clock tomorrow, because Luka has a spelling test and I want to be ready to practise the words with him?" The assistant said, "Reminder set for four o'clock tomorrow: spelling practice with Luka." Dragan thanked it. When the evening came, he was ready with a list of words and a pencil.

name: find_radio_station
does: Finds the station that plays the show or music you want and tunes the radio to it, even if you are up a ladder or digging in the garden with your hands full, and checks that it is the correct one.
inputs: the kind of show or music, or the station name or number
people say:
- Put on the football
- Get me the weather news
- Find that jazz station
- Tune to ninety-eight point five
- I want to hear the traffic report

remind me to water the carrots
remnd me at six to water the plants
Don't let me forget the balcony plants tonight
ping me when I get home about the carrots

remind me tonigt to water the balcony

Wouter's shop was quiet that afternoon, and nobody had come in for an hour. He looked at the height of the empty shelves and then at the clock. "It's so silent in here," he said to the speaker behind the counter. The assistant understood. "Would you like some music or the radio?" it asked. "The radio," said Wouter, and the assistant tuned to his usual station. He typed the new prices on his laptop while a huge laugh came out of the speaker from the morning show. Soon a customer came in, humming along, and bought two books.

Where is my order?
When does my food get here?
Is it coming in less than twenty minutes?
Has the driver left yet?
I'm starving, how much longer is my delivery?
Can you check my dinner order? It's urgent, I have a meeting soon
Track my food, please
Is my order late?

Person: Fair enough. Thanks.

Book a haircut for my daughter
I need an appointment for my girl at the Mill Street salon

book hair, mill street

See if the salon has room tomorrow and book it if they do

Ahmed lay in bed with the blanket over his head. For a fraction of a minute he did not want to move. Then a sudden cold wind rattled the window. "It's freezing out there, and the windscreen must be covered in ice," he said to his phone, still lying down. The assistant understood and started the car's engine and the heater. "The car is warming up," it said. "It will be ready in ten minutes." Ahmed smiled, closed his eyes for a bit longer, and then got up to find his coat. When he went out, the windscreen was clear.

table for two, tonight

Ananya was new to the city, and tonight she wanted to cook dal for her friends. The recipe she had made food for two people. "Make this recipe for four, but don't change the spoons into cups, I only have spoons," she said to her phone. The assistant answered, "Done. For four, you need two tablespoons of oil and one and a half cups of lentils. I left the spoons as they are." Ananya counted the plates. She had four, which was the maximum she owned. The assistant added a note: cook for thirty minutes. The dal tasted like home.

people say:

- I'm going to sleep, turn it off later
- Fade out the song after twenty minutes
- Music off at midnight
- Don't let the music play all night

Tonight after dinner, Freya sat down with her tablet and a cup of tea. She was a retired teacher, and she liked to check her money every week. "Show me how much I spent on food this month," she said. The assistant read out a number. "Is it true that I spent more than last month?" she asked. "Yes, about ten percent more," the assistant said. Freya sighed. Her grandson's drum lessons had cost a lot too. "I'd like to keep my food spending under two hundred next month," she said. The assistant saved the limit and promised to warn her.

When a courier brings a package, you often have to sign for it. Today many people sign by swiping a finger across a small screen. If you are not home, the courier leaves a card, or puts the parcel with a neighbour. People change this all the time. They say "Leave it with my neighbour," "Hold my parcel until Monday," or "Don't ring the bell, the baby is asleep." Some parcels are flat boxes with a shelf inside, and the screws come in a small bag. Letters just go into the mailbox, and you open the door of the box with a small key.

Caleb was driving home with the baby asleep in the back seat. He did not want to look at his phone. "Could you please text my cousin Jo that I'll be twenty minutes late, because the baby just fell asleep in the car and I don't want to wake her by stopping?" he asked quietly. The assistant said, "I'll send Jo a message: running twenty minutes late. Is that okay?" Caleb said yes. The assistant dimmed the screen so the light would not bother the baby. A strong wind pushed the car a little, but she slept on. Jo wrote back with a thumbs up.

Air conditioning takes warm air out of a room and blows in cool air. A fan only moves the air, so the room does not get cooler, but you feel better. People change the temperature or the speed all day. They say "Make it a bit cooler," "Set the air conditioner to twenty-four," or "Turn the fan down, it's too loud." My old unit was hard to use, but the new one can connect to a phone. The manual document has a long list of buttons. Most people just say "Turn on the cooling at five" and come home to a nice room.

A packing list helps you remember what to take when you go camping. It might say: tent, sleeping bag, water, snacks, and a yellow raincoat that fits in your pocket. The weather in the hills can change fast, so people check it before they leave. They say "What's the weather on Saturday up at the lake?" or "Add a torch to my packing list." If the plan changes, they say "Move the trip to next weekend." On the trail, if you will be late, you can text a friend to say where you are, so nobody worries.

Miriam stood at the bus stop with her two small children and a heavy bag. "Don't buy a day ticket, I only need a single one for each of us," she told the assistant on her phone. "Okay, I'll buy three single tickets for the number twelve bus," it said. Miriam wanted to be sure the stop was correct, so she asked, "What is the name of the stop near the museum?" The assistant spelled it out slowly, letter by letter. The tickets appeared on the screen just as the bus came around the corner, and the children cheered.

Someone going away in two weeks, with a dark sky outside every evening, wants an alert if a camera sees something wrong at home, so they won't wait and wonder.
Tell me if anything looks odd at home
Alert me if the camera sees someone
In two weeks I'll be away, watch the front door
send a warning if the alarm goes off
I don't want to worry on holiday, can you let me know if the sensors notice movement?
Could you please turn on the motion alerts from the day I leave in two weeks?
keep an eye on the house

Hassan was a cook, and on Sunday he planned the meals for the week. His sister called while he was chopping onions, but he let it ring. "Plan dinners for the week, with half as much meat as last week," he said to the assistant. The assistant answered with five dinners: red lentil soup, rice with beans, and fish on Thursday. "Dim the kitchen lights a little, I'm tired," Hassan said. The assistant dimmed them. He looked at the list and liked it. Then he asked it to make a shopping list from the plan and send it to his phone.

Meera was not good with technology, but she was practising. Today she was excited because she wanted to call her son Raj all by herself. A big spider sat on the kitchen wall, and she did not want to go near it. "Could you please call my son Raj, because I am afraid of pressing the wrong button, and I want to tell him about this spider?" she said slowly to her phone. The assistant answered, "Calling Raj now." Meera held the phone to her ear and heard it ring. Raj picked up, and they laughed together about the spider.

Person: Play something for me.
Assistant: What kind of music would you like?
Person: Something with a deep voice. I'm planting bulbs and I want music for fifteen minutes.
Assistant: Do you want songs or just an instrument?
Person: Songs. Is there a difference in how long they are?
Assistant: Most songs are about three minutes, so fifteen minutes is about five songs. I'll play a playlist of deep voices.
Person: Good. And close the music app when it's done.
Assistant: I can stop the music after fifteen minutes. I can't close the app, sorry.

Hugo sat in his armchair and felt a bit sick. His head spun when he stood up. He did not want to scare anyone, but he did not feel safe alone. "Could you please call my daughter, because I feel dizzy and I would like her to know?" he said to the assistant on the table. "Calling Anna now," said the assistant. Hugo took his pills, which were the size of a coin, and drank a glass of water. His coffee filter was still on the counter. Anna answered and said she would come in ten minutes, and Hugo felt calmer.

Someone going away wants the lights to turn on by a schedule so the house looks like someone is home.
light timer
Fake being home
Tell the lamps to come on at dusk
Turn the lights on and off while we're away

Could you please set the lights on a schedule while I'm gone?
lights, every evening

Person: Add a new contact, please. My hands are wet from the garden, so I'll speak.
Assistant: Sure. What is the name?
Person: Marta. She was in my class in the year two thousand.
Assistant: Got it, Marta. What is her phone number?
Person: Oh, I don't have it with me.
Assistant: That's okay. I saved Marta without a number. Tell me when you find it.
Person: Make the text size bigger, too. And unmute my phone so I can hear her call.
Assistant: I made the text bigger and turned the sound on.

Elif the gardener held up her best tomatoes. They had won a prize at the village fair, and one was tiny but perfect. She wanted a picture. "Please take a photo of my tomatoes with the front camera, because I want to send it to my sister, and my hands are dirty," she said to her phone. The assistant answered, "Taking a photo in three, two, one." The picture came out bright. Elif peeled the dirt off her glove and said, "Send it to my sister Aylin." The assistant sent the photo, and soon Aylin wrote back with three hearts.

Person: I just finished a night shift and I'm baking bread. Start my podcast and set a timer for the bread.
Assistant: How long should the timer be?
Person: Forty minutes.
Assistant: Timer set for forty minutes. Which podcast should I play?
Person: The one about gardens. Also, increase the oven to two hundred and twenty, just temporary, until the crust is brown.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't change your oven. It isn't connected to me. I started the garden podcast and the timer is running.
Person: Fine, I'll turn it up myself.

Zana was new to the city, and her baby was only three months old. It was late at night, and she could not remember what had happened at the last feeding. "Tell me when the next feeding is due and start the baby monitor," she said to her phone. The assistant answered, "The last feeding was at eight, so the next is around eleven. The monitor is on." Zana held the baby, skin to skin, and whispered thanks. The assistant said it would send a message to her phone if the baby made a sound. Whatever might happen, she felt calmer.
